item.title: Beyond the Burn: How Orangetheory Is Shaping the Future of Studio Workouts
item.description: Orangetheory Fitness is redefining the future of workouts with smarter tech, strength-based programming, and community-driven studios built for what’s next.

item.title: Rewiring Rest: How Somnee Is Changing the Way We Sleep
item.description: Somnee CEO Tim Rosa shares how next-gen sleep wearables, tACS technology, and data-driven insights are redefining recovery and performance.

item.title: IPO to Innovation: Why Weshop Is One of Ecommerce’s Most Watched Companies
item.description: After a blockbuster IPO, Weshop is redefining ecommerce by giving users equity, influence, and a stake in the platform’s success.

item.description: The U.S. has collected more than $200 billion this year from new tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump since early 2025.

item.title: Is Uncle Sam Going Full Silicon Valley?
item.description: The Trump administration unveiled the “U.S. Tech Force,” a new initiative deploying about 1,000 engineers and tech specialists across the federal government.

item.title: No Driver, No Problem? Tesla’s Robotaxi Moment Hits Austin
item.description: Tesla says it is now testing fully driverless Robotaxi vehicles in Austin, Texas, with no humans on board, according to CEO Elon Musk.

item.title: Trump Vs. The BBC: Panorama Drama Goes Prime Time
item.description: President Trump filed a defamation lawsuit against the BBC in Miami federal court, seeking at least $5 billion in damages over a Panorama documentary.

item.title: PayPal Eyes a Banking Upgrade
item.description: PayPal said it has applied for approval to form PayPal Bank, a move that would allow it to offer loans to small businesses and expand its financial services.

item.title: Merriam-Webster: “Slop” is the Word of the Year
item.description: Merriam-Webster named “slop” its 2025 word of the year, reflecting rising skepticism about low-quality AI-generated content flooding the internet.

item.title: Wall Street drifts lower following mixed data on the economy
item.description: The U.S. stock market is drifting lower following mixed data on the economy’s strength. The S&P 500 fell 0.4% Tuesday and remains a bit below its all-time high set last week. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 271 points, and the Nasdaq composite was mostly unchanged. Treasury yields eased a bit after the reports on the U.S. job market, retail sales and business activity did little to clear uncertainty about where the Federal Reserve may take interest rates next year.
